overall.headline: Stagflation-shaped risk, not a credit blowup
overall.label: Yellow
overall.text: Stocks sit near record highs while the 10-yr Treasury touched 5.34%, its highest since 2002, and Brent holds above $100 with Hormuz disrupted. Hiring has nearly stalled. Credit is softening at the edges but not breaking. Expect a slower, choppier market, not a crash call.

powder.action: Keep new 401k contributions flowing to Bond Plus. No transfers in either direction. The S&P 500 Equity Index is within ~1% of its high, nowhere near the 10% pullback that opens the deploy zone, and cash-like yields near 5% pay you to wait.
powder.label: Build — steady
powder.note: Check what Bond Plus actually holds. If it is an intermediate bond fund, it carries interest-rate risk: rising yields push its price down, and that's the main threat right now. A stable-value or money-market option in your plan would be closer to true dry powder. Not financial advice.

changes: First report; this sets the baseline for future month-over-month comparisons.

macro.name: Treasury yields
macro.note: 10-yr at 5.3%. A disorderly move past 5.5% would pressure stocks and bond funds together.

macro.name: Oil & Strait of Hormuz
macro.note: Brent above $100 is driving inflation fears. A peace deal is the single biggest upside catalyst.

macro.name: Fed path
macro.note: Hiked in September. Weak jobs lowered October hike odds, but a hot CPI reopens it.

macro.name: Labor market
macro.note: +29K jobs, 4.2% unemployment, with downward revisions. The Sahm rule has not triggered.

macro.name: Credit
macro.note: Junk spreads at 294bp (widest since April); CCC spreads at highs since 2023. Heavy AI-related debt issuance.

macro.name: Crypto sentiment
macro.note: Bitcoin about a third below its peak while stocks sit near records. Watch for a breakdown as a risk-appetite warning.

outlook.text: Q3 earnings season, September CPI, the late-October FOMC, US-Iran/Hormuz news and the Nov 3 midterms all land inside the window. Expect volatility within a range; a peace deal is the main upside surprise.

Strong earnings growth is fighting 5%+ yields. The multiple has already compressed from ~22x toward ~19–21x. Expect flat-to-single-digit returns, with downside skew if oil keeps inflation and yields rising.
Record forward earnings carry the index higher over a year if margins hold. Valuation caps the upside. A 10–15% pullback somewhere in the year is a normal event and the likely deploy window.

pullback.note: ATH is approximate. The deploy zone starts at a 10% pullback (≈6,930), and a 20% pullback (≈6,160) is a major opportunity.

swans: A Hormuz escalation, or a sudden oil collapse on a peace deal (either direction moves markets)
Foreign selling of US Treasuries causing a disorderly bond market
An AI-capex debt unwind (~$600B of AI-related debt issued this year)

green: US-Iran deal reopens Hormuz and Brent drops below $85
Breadth broadens to small and mid caps
An S&P pullback of 10%+ with credit still calm, which opens the deploy zone
red: Unemployment at 4.5% or higher, or the Sahm rule near 0.5
A hot CPI that forces an October hike
10-yr breaks above ~5.5% in a disorderly way
